reviewers.summary: The analysis applies partial correlation with a categorical covariate (treatment), which is methodologically unsound. The report lacks essential diagnostics, missing data handling, and effect size interpretation. Raw data is inaccessible for verification. Revise with appropriate regression methods and comprehensive diagnostics.

findings.title: Partial correlation inapplicable when adjusting for a categorical variable
evidenceRefs: stats-run.json: estimates adjusted_for includes 'treatment', a categorical variable
findings.whyItMatters: Partial correlation requires all variables to be continuous; including a categorical variable violates assumptions and yields unreliable results.
findings.actionableFix: Use linear regression with treatment as a factor variable and report partial effect sizes (e.g., standardized beta) or ANCOVA. Alternatively, compute partial correlation within treatment subgroups if appropriate.
findings.deterministicVerification: Verify variable type of 'treatment' in the dataset; if categorical, the method is invalid.

findings.title: No diagnostic checks for partial correlation assumptions
findings.whyItMatters: Without assessing linearity, normality, homoscedasticity, and outliers, the reported correlation may be spurious or misleading.
findings.actionableFix: Produce residual plots, Q-Q plots, and influence diagnostics for the underlying regressions. If assumptions are violated, consider robust or non-parametric alternatives.
findings.deterministicVerification: Check for existence of diagnostic plots or statistical tests in the run artifacts; currently absent.

findings.title: Complete-case analysis without missing data assessment
findings.whyItMatters: If missingness is not completely at random, the estimate may be biased, and the sample may not represent the intended population.
findings.actionableFix: Report the proportion of missing data, compare observed characteristics between complete and incomplete cases, and consider multiple imputation or sensitivity analyses.
findings.deterministicVerification: Check whether a missing-data analysis file exists in the run artifacts; none is present.

findings.title: Report emphasizes statistical significance over effect size
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md: no interpretation of correlation magnitude or confidence interval
findings.whyItMatters: The extremely small p-value may overshadow the practical importance of the effect; readers need context for the correlation coefficient.
findings.actionableFix: Report 95% confidence interval for the partial correlation and discuss its magnitude in domain terms (e.g., using Cohen's thresholds). Include caution about p-value misinterpretation.
findings.deterministicVerification: Check if confidence interval is reported in the manuscript or companion tables; currently missing.

findings.title: No discussion of unmeasured confounding or sensitivity analysis
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md: Limitations section mentions only data bound limits, not confounding
findings.whyItMatters: Even for local evidence, residual confounding can invalidate the association; readers cannot assess the strength of the evidence without this discussion.
findings.actionableFix: Add a section recognizing potential unmeasured confounders (e.g., disease severity, comorbidities) and, if possible, a sensitivity analysis like E-value.
findings.deterministicVerification: Check if the manuscript mentions residual confounding; it currently does not.

findings.title: Scatterplot shows bivariate relationship, not partial correlation
evidenceRefs: figure-qa.json: scatterplot of outcome_cont vs severity
figure caption: 'Scatterplot for the two variables used in the correlation run.'
findings.whyItMatters: The figure may mislead readers into interpreting the plotted association as the adjusted partial correlation.
findings.actionableFix: Replace with partial residual (added variable) plots that display the relationship after adjusting for covariates.
findings.deterministicVerification: Check the figure; current scatterplot does not account for age and treatment.

findings.title: Limitations mention 'No estimate-like records' despite presence of estimates
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md: 'No estimate-like records were available for p-value/effect-size checks.'
stats-run.json: contains an estimate for severity
findings.whyItMatters: This contradictory statement confuses readers and suggests a templating error.
findings.actionableFix: Remove or correct the sentence to reflect that an estimate is available.
findings.deterministicVerification: Check the manuscript text against the stats-run output; the estimate exists.

findings.title: Raw data not available for independent verification
evidenceRefs: run directory artifacts do not include the original dataset
reproducibility section lists 14 artifacts, none are the data
findings.whyItMatters: Without access to the underlying data, the reported results cannot be fully reproduced or validated.
findings.actionableFix: Provide the de-identified dataset (if permitted) or a detailed summary statistics table that allows partial verification.
findings.deterministicVerification: Check for a data file (e.g., CSV) in the run artifacts; it is absent.

reviewers.summary: The manuscript fails to report the primary result (partial correlation and p-value) in the Results section. Model diagnostics are missing. No confidence interval is provided. Critical reporting and review gaps prevent use as evidence.

findings.title: Primary analysis result absent from manuscript
findings.whyItMatters: Readers cannot assess the study's main finding without the partial correlation estimate and its uncertainty in the manuscript body.
findings.actionableFix: Add the partial correlation coefficient (0.654), p-value, and a confidence interval for the correlation to the Results section, with appropriate cautious interpretation.
findings.deterministicVerification: Check that manuscript Results section contains numeric estimate and uncertainty from stats-run.json.

findings.title: No model diagnostics for partial correlation assumptions
findings.whyItMatters: Partial correlation assumes linearity, normality of residuals, and homoscedasticity. Violations can invalidate the estimate.
findings.actionableFix: Provide diagnostic plots (e.g., residual vs. fitted, Q-Q plot) and tests, or explicitly state that assumptions were checked and satisfied. Include these in supplementary or main text.

findings.title: Confidence interval for partial correlation missing
findings.whyItMatters: The point estimate alone gives no sense of precision; a 95% CI is essential for interpretability.
findings.actionableFix: Compute and report a 95% CI for the partial correlation (e.g., via Fisher transformation) alongside the p-value.

findings.title: Extremely small p-value may mislead readers
findings.whyItMatters: A p-value of 1e-30 could be misinterpreted as a measure of effect size or practical importance. Caution is needed.
findings.actionableFix: Add explicit statement that the p-value does not equate to effect size and that with large n small effects can be significant; emphasize the moderate correlation coefficient.

findings.title: Study not placed in context of existing research
findings.whyItMatters: Without references or comparison, the local evidence cannot be interpreted against known associations.
findings.actionableFix: Add a brief literature review or clarify that this is an isolated exploratory analysis with no external validation.

findings.title: Scatterplot figure not accessible for reviewer
findings.whyItMatters: The scatterplot is the only visual check of the raw relationship; its absence prevents assessment of outliers or non-linearity.
findings.actionableFix: Include the actual scatterplot image in the manuscript or ensure it is available during review.

missingEvidence: Raw data or analysis code for reproducibility
Diagnostic plots for partial correlation assumptions
Confidence interval for the partial correlation
